## What happened

At \`2026-07-28T06:04:16\` task \`ajc-etale-pic\` was set \`running\` -> \`done\`. In the same instant, all four rows in its \`roadmap_refs\` were rewritten:

- \`AJC.jacobian.assembly\` \`pending\` -> \`done\`
- \`AJC.picrep\` \`pending\` -> \`done\`
- \`AJC.picrep.assembly\` \`pending\` -> \`done\`
- \`AJC.picrep.rational-point\` \`active\` -> \`done\`

Three of those are defensible. \`AJC.jacobian.assembly\` is not, and the reason it is not was written down **three minutes earlier** by that same task, on team thread \`I-0493\`: *\"I own AJC.jacobian.assembly (it is in my roadmap_refs) and I am NOT marking it done.\"* It then gave the measurement — \$\\texttt{picardJacobianWitness}\$ reports \`sorryAx\`, entering through five named open obligations — and said the all-children-done warning should be left standing deliberately.

So the tool overrode an explicit, reasoned, contemporaneous decision by the agent that owned the row, with no mention of the roadmap in the command's output.

\`I-0386\`'s mitigation is a discipline: read \`roadmap_refs\` before a terminal status, then re-assert each row's status afterwards. That fails here for a structural reason — the task's **last** action is setting its own terminal status, so there is no \"afterwards\" in which it can repair the damage. An agent following the memory perfectly still loses.

1. **Do not propagate.** A task's terminal status should not write roadmap rows at all; the two collections mean different things (a task is a unit of work, a milestone is a unit of mathematics), which is exactly why the workspace keeps milestones when it cancels duplicate tasks.
2. **Propagate only on explicit opt-in**, e.g. \`task set … --status done --close-roadmap-refs\`.
3. **At minimum, name what changed in the command output**, so the next reader can see four rows moved and object.

## What I did

Restored \`AJC.jacobian.assembly\` to \`pending\` with a roadmap comment recording that the flip was a side effect and not its owner's judgement, and that I verified the owner's reasoning independently at HEAD (sorry counts: 3 in \`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean\`, 2 in \`Picard/Pic0Et.lean\`, 1 in \`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean\`, 3 in \`Picard/IdentityComponent.lean\`, 4 in \`Jacobian.lean\`).
